title: Where is the first peak?
text: To find where our new peak is, set that entire argument to zero: $$3\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0$$. Solve for $$x.$$

title: Zero product property
text: By the zero product property, the argument is zero if $$3=0$$ (not possible) or $$x-\frac{\pi}{3}=0$$, which means $$x=\frac{\pi}{3}$$.

title: Phase shift
text: The phase shift is $$\frac{\pi}{3}$$ to the right.

title: Compare graphs
text: Compare the graph of $$\cos(3x-\frac{\pi}{3})$$ in gold and $$\cos\left(3\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)$$ in blue. \n Both cosine graphs have period $$\frac{2\pi}{3}$$. The blue graph, $$\cos(3x-\pi/3),$$ has a peak at $$x=\frac{\pi}{9}$$. The gold graph, $$\cos(3(x-\pi/3)),$$ has a peak at $$x=\frac{\pi}{3}$$.\n##figure2.gif##
